claims.text: Trích II.1 (hai đoạn, nối bằng […]) khớp nguyên văn

sources.quote: If all mankind minus one, were of one opinion, and only one person were of the contrary opinion, mankind would be no more justified in silencing that one person
if wrong, they lose, what is almost as great a benefit, the clearer perception and livelier impression of truth, produced by its collision with error
it is robbing the human race; posterity as well as the existing generation; those who dissent from the opinion, still more than those who hold it

claims.text: Trích II.2, II.3, II.6 khớp nguyên văn

sources.quote: We can never be sure that the opinion we are endeavouring to stifle is a false opinion; and if we were sure, stifling it would be an evil still.
All silencing of discussion is an assumption of infallibility.

There is the greatest difference between presuming an opinion to be true, because, with every opportunity for contesting it, it has not been refuted, and assuming its truth for the purpose of not permitting its refutation.

claims.text: Câu cuối là lời Mill đáp một phản bác mà chính ông nêu ra (II.5): chính quyền ... đánh thuế hay tuyên chiến

sources.quote: they have laid on bad taxes, made unjust wars. Ought we therefore to lay on no taxes
Complete liberty of contradicting and disproving our opinion, is the very condition which justifies us in assuming its truth for purposes of action

claims.text: Trích II.21 và II.23 khớp nguyên văn

sources.quote: however true it may be, if it is not fully, frequently, and fearlessly discussed, it will be held as a dead dogma, not a living truth
He who knows only his own side of the case, knows little of that.

claims.text: Mill nhắc 'thuyết địa tâm thay cho nhật tâm' (II.23)

sources.quote: some geocentric theory instead of heliocentric, some phlogiston instead of oxygen
But there is a commoner case than either of these; when the conflicting doctrines, instead of being one true and the other false, share the truth between them
Popular opinions, on subjects not palpable to sense, are often true, but seldom or never the whole truth.

claims.text: Rousseau: thế kỷ 18, nghịch lý nổ ra 'như những quả bom'; quan điểm đương thời gần sự thật hơn nhưng Rousseau giữ phần sự thật họ thiếu (II.35)

sources.quote: with what a salutary shock did the paradoxes of Rousseau explode like bombshells
the current opinions were on the whole farther from the truth than Rousseau's were; on the contrary, they were nearer to it

claims.text: Niềm tin đúng mà không qua tranh luận giống một cơ bắp không bao giờ vận động

sources.quote: it will be held as a dead dogma, not a living truth
sources.where: II.21; hình ảnh cơ bắp là ví von của bài, không phải của Mill, và không bị gán cho Mill

notes: Gutenberg.org tạm bảo trì khi kiểm; đọc ebook 34901 qua bản lưu web.archive.org (cùng ebook, cùng bản Walter Scott/Courtney). Ghi chú: ví von 'cơ bắp' là của bài, không đóng khung như lời Mill; chấp nhận.
